payload.comment: Reporting stage is arithmetically and structurally sound. All invariants verified: confusion-matrix row sums match per-class supports (total 7180); accuracy 6279/7180 = 0.874513; balanced_accuracy = macro_recall = 0.852848; selective_risk identity (1 − 0.980371 = 0.019629); abstain count 0.47493 × 7180 = 3410; total errors 901 = 7180 × (1 − 0.874513); accuracy_delta 0.874513 − 0.840251 = 0.034262; common seed 47 and split fingerprint 9afc9ed… consistent across baseline, agentic, and comparison reports; test lock enforced (test_metrics_used = false in search). No deterministic findings. The LLM-raised issues are valid observations about model behaviour and analysis scope, not reporting errors: (1) the 12.1 pp validation→test accuracy gap and the 27.5 pp abstention-coverage gap (80.0 % → 52.5 %) are real generalisation properties that downstream consumers must be aware of, but they are correctly reported, not misreported; (2) OOD evaluation is limited to controlled Gaussian-noise corruption (σ 0.15/0.25/0.4) with AUROC 0.89 test vs 0.995 validation—this scope limitation is transparently stated in the artefact; (3) per-class weaknesses (stroma recall 45.6 %, smooth-muscle F1 0.632, adipose→smooth-muscle confusion 21 %) are accurately reflected in the confusion matrix and per-class table; (4) minor documentation gaps (rotate90 augmentation, early_stopping_patience = 3, 'standardize' without per-channel qualifier, transformer params in CNN config) are inherited from upstream stages and do not affect reporting correctness. The comparison report omits macro-F1 delta and significance testing, which would strengthen the analysis but are not required for internal consistency. All 38 artefact versions are accounted for; 105 decision events logged. The reporting faithfully and accurately presents the evaluation results. No corrections required; proceed to finalisation.
llm_issues: Validation-to-test accuracy gap of 12.1 pp (0.9958 → 0.8745) is a material generalisation risk that should be prominently flagged for downstream consumers
Abstention coverage guarantee does not transfer: 80.0 % validation → 52.5 % test (27.5 pp gap); operational systems expecting ~80 % coverage will see ~52.5 %
OOD evaluation scope limited to controlled Gaussian-noise corruption (σ 0.15/0.25/0.4); real-world domain shift, novel tissue types, and imaging artefacts unverified
Cancer-associated stroma recall 45.6 % and smooth-muscle F1 0.632 on test are substantially below validation-level performance; these confusions were not visible in validation metrics
Adipose→smooth-muscle confusion (283/1338 = 21 %) is the single largest error source on test
Comparison report omits macro-F1 delta (+0.0559), balanced-accuracy comparison, and any statistical significance test on the 3.4 pp accuracy delta
Model-capacity asymmetry (tiny_cnn depth-2/hidden-16 vs residual_cnn depth-4/hidden-80) not discussed as a potential confound on the comparison delta
Augmentation 'rotate90' (90° discrete) deviates from research-recommended small-angle jitter; empirically validated but under-documented for reproducibility
early_stopping_patience = 3 is below the 5–8 range recommended in research notes; low risk given convergence but limited margin for slower re-runs
Normalization labeled 'standardize' without explicit per-channel qualifier; implementation should be confirmed
Transformer-specific parameters (num_heads, mlp_ratio, pooling, positional_encoding, tokenizer_layers) present in residual_cnn config; likely shared-schema no-ops but unconfirmed
